title: Radix-eight pointer trie as the in-context store, with a bracket bit word
summary: Addresses are spelled as three base-8 digits and stored along paths of a trie whose nodes are allocated from a fixed pool of 96. The node at the end of a path holds the item written there; reading spells the probe's digits and follows the pointers. A bit word records the open bracket types. Tasks are given in a fixed episode format: copy (a start mark, L symbols, a separator, then the copy); recall (K address-item pairs, then each address once as a probe); nesting (two bracket types, predict each legal closer); two-hop lookup (table g as pairs, table f as pairs, then probes x answered f(g(x))); and chained assignments (variables bound to variables or to final symbols, then a probe variable).
core_idea: Spell each address in base-8 digits along a pointer trie drawn from a fixed node pool, hold the item at the end node, and read by walking the probe's digits.

state.name: T
state.meaning: Pool of 96 nodes; each node has 8 child pointers (0 means none) and one item field; node 0 is the root.

state.name: f
state.meaning: Index of the next unused node of the pool.

state.name: bw
state.meaning: Bracket bit word: open bracket types as binary digits, innermost lowest, at most H = 20 bits.

state.name: pi
state.meaning: Position counter of the string phase.

update.name: digits
update.plain: the address code kappa(z_t) in 0..511 (pi for strings, id for pairs, 64 + id for the second table) is split into base-8 digits delta_1 delta_2 delta_3, with delta_k = floor(kappa / 8^(3-k)) mod 8

update.name: walk and allocate
update.latex: u \leftarrow T[u].\mathrm{child}[\delta_k] \text{ or a new node } f \leftarrow f + 1
update.plain: start at the root node u = 0; for k = 1, 2, 3: if the child pointer T[u].child[delta_k] is 0, allocate node f, set the pointer to f and f = f + 1; move u to that child

update.name: item
update.plain: store the item code 2 id(item) + lambda_t at the end node u, lambda_t = 1 for a final symbol

update.name: bracket bit word
update.plain: push an opener of type b: bw = 2 bw + b; pop at a closer: bw = floor(bw / 2)

readout.name: walk
readout.plain: follow the pointers of the probe's three digits from the root; the item at the end node is the answer (none if a pointer is 0)

readout.name: chains and two hops
readout.plain: a chained assignment walks again with the named variable while the item's flag is 0, at most 8 times; f(g(x)) walks 64 + id(x), then the result

readout.name: closer
readout.plain: the legal closer has the type in the lowest bit of the bracket bit word

learning.description: Symbol roles are learned as the most probable role under a posterior that starts from a uniform prior over roles and multiplies in, for each of m example episodes, the likelihood of the observed answers under each role (1 if consistent, a small floor otherwise).
learning.few_shot_argument: Every symbol's role is pinned by a single consistent episode, because any other role mispredicts at least one answer there; m = 6 episodes per task leave a posterior concentrated on the true roles in the small cases.

complexity.constants_notes: Three pointer steps, at most three allocations and one item write per symbol; reads take at most 8 walks of three steps. The pool of 96 nodes of 9 words, the bit word and two counters are fixed in n.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Posterior over symbol roles from m example episodes.

prediction.statement: With m = 6 example episodes of a task (copy and recall at size up to 4, nesting at depth 2, two-hop lookup at table size up to 4, chained assignments of length up to 2), the learned roles are exact and the task is solved with accuracy 1.0 on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator (L = 8, 32, 64)
capabilities.prediction: Hand-set construction: symbol i is stored under the code pi = i and read back by walking pi = 1..L after the separator; exact at L = 8, 32 and 64 (at most 1 + 8 + 64 = 73 nodes).
Hand-set construction: each address is stored under its identity; exact at K = 8, 32 and 64.
The bracket bit word holds the open types and its lowest bit names the legal closer: exact at depths 2, 4, 8 and 16 with H = 20.

capabilities.task: two-hop lookup f(g(x)) with tables of size 4, 16, 32, and chained assignments of length 1, 4, 8
capabilities.prediction: Table g under codes 64..95 and table f under 0..31, two walks per probe; exact at sizes 4, 16 and 32 (at most 1 + 8 + 2 + 64 nodes). One stored item per assignment and at most 8 walks per probe; exact at chain lengths 1, 4 and 8.

Derived limit for nesting: an H-bit word distinguishes at most 2^H stacks, while depth-D bracket prefixes of two types have 2^D distinct stacks, so the share of stacks whose every closer is predicted right is at most 2^(H-D) and exact prediction fails for every depth D < H; with H = 20 no configuration is exact at depth 19 or below.
The role posterior learns every small case from m = 6 episodes on three seeds.

falsifiers: Walking a stored address returns an item other than the one last written under it.
The node pool is exhausted before 64 distinct codes are stored.

toy_example.description: Storing three codes in a small trie and walking one back; the bracket bit word after three pushes and a pop.
